title: Winery Address or Tasting Room? Confirm the Right Entrance
description: A winery name or vineyard pin may not identify your tasting destination. Match the booked experience, visitor address and entrance before planning the ride.
cta: Build the wine-country route from confirmed visitor addresses.
image_alt: An anonymous wine-country estate with a gravel visitor driveway leading toward a stone-and-wood building beside a separate vineyard track.
body:
Use the visitor address and arrival instructions for your booked tasting experience when planning a winery ride. A wine label, vineyard location, production facility or general brand search is not enough to identify where guests should arrive. Match the property and experience on the reservation to the winery's current official directions, then share that destination with the transportation provider.

This matters before estimating the day: a different property or entrance can change the route between appointments. A map result confirms that a place exists; it does not confirm your reservation, visitor access or the correct check-in point.

Start with the experience confirmation

Record the winery name, exact property or tasting-room name, booked experience, local date, appointment time and reservation name. Use the street address attached to that experience. If the confirmation and a general contact page disagree, ask the winery which arrival instructions apply to your appointment.

Brands can have more than one visitor destination. HALL's official site, for example, lists HALL St. Helena and HALL Rutherford separately. Sending only 'HALL' leaves the property unresolved. Match the reservation before putting either stop on the transport itinerary; a tasting at one location is not permission to visit another.

Use the winery's visitor directions

A useful destination record includes the street address and the winery's own last-step instructions, if supplied. Avoid replacing them with an attractive vineyard photo, a winery office pin or a location saved from an earlier visit.

  • Domaine Carneros labels 1240 Duhig Road, Napa, as its tasting-room address. Use the tasting reservation and current directions together rather than searching for a vineyard name from a bottle.
  • Jordan lists 1474 Alexander Valley Road, Healdsburg, and gives directions to its entrance. Its visitor experiences are offered by appointment. The entrance is a useful arrival detail; it does not establish availability for your chosen date.

These are location examples, not Koast partnerships or recommendations of a particular appointment. Verify your own confirmation and any new instructions directly with the winery. Do not rely on an old address saved in a past itinerary.

Make an arrival card for each stop

Before asking for transportation, build a short stop record that both the organizer and the traveler can read:

  • Booked destination: winery, property/tasting-room name and experience.
  • Location: full visitor address and official directions link.
  • Arrival: appointment time, winery-requested check-in lead time and meeting/check-in point.
  • Access: any confirmed gate, driveway, group arrival or vehicle instructions relevant to the visit.
  • Departure: where the group should meet again and who will contact the transportation provider if the appointment changes.

If the winery has not provided an entrance detail, mark it as a question. Do not invent a gate code, choose a vineyard service track or assume a larger vehicle can turn around at the property. Give any access instructions only to the people coordinating the trip, rather than posting private access information publicly.

A small location change can change the day

Illustrative example: a group has listed a brand's general winery address, but its confirmation names a different tasting room. Correct the actual destination before finalizing the next appointment. Ask the transportation provider to review the stop order and timing, and ask the winery about any arrival adjustment. Neither a familiar brand name nor a short-looking line on a map proves that the original schedule still works.

If a tasting moves after transport is arranged, identify the old and new stops, the affected appointment and any changed party or luggage details. Obtain acknowledgment of the revised route and applicable quote or terms. A tasting-room change does not automatically amend the car reservation. Our tasting and transportation reservation guide explains the two confirmations; the tasting-versus-tour guide helps identify which experience you actually booked.

Check access again before setting off

Read the winery's latest message before travel and check Caltrans QuickMap for current road conditions. A road alert and a winery's visitor entrance are different pieces of information: neither proves the other is accessible. Ask the winery if its arrival instructions need adjustment during a local closure or access change; do not promise a detour duration.

For a new wine-country journey, explore Koast wine tours and include the confirmed visitor addresses, appointment times, passenger count and luggage in your quote request. For an existing Koast ride, use your reservation confirmation or agreed day-of-trip contact and obtain acknowledgment of changes; a new quote does not amend that ride.
